sentences.text:
Pawan Kumar Surana & Ors vs Bishnu Prasad Samanta on 12
January, 2017

Author: Indrajit Chatterjee
Bench: Indrajit Chatterjee
 1
12-1-2017
Item no.31 aks..
C.R.R. 3223 of 2012 Pawan Kumar Surana & Ors.
Vs. Bishnu Prasad Samanta Mr. Debashis Roy Mr. Vivek Jhunjhunwala Mr. Anirban Tarafdar ... for
the petitioners.
Mr. Gopal Chandra Das Mrs. Rituparna Sarkar ... for the opposite party.

It is submitted by Mr. Roy, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners that the present accused persons, namely, Pawan Kumar Surana, Shanti Kumar Surana and Vijay Dwivedi ought not to have been implicated in Complaint Case No.6D of 2010, now pending before the learned Municipal Magistrate and Metropolitan Magistrate, 3rd Court, Calcutta under Section 16(1)a (i) and under Section 12 of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954.

He took me to running page no. 20 to show that one Joydeep Nath (accused no. 1), Operation Head of M/s. Middleton Hotels Pvt. Ltd. was nominated by the company by a Resolution passed at their meeting held on 22/12/2008 at Kolkata to be a person in charge and responsible to the said company for the conduct of the business of the said company or establishment.

He further submitted that the said application was received by the Chief Municipal Health Officer,
Kolkata on 02/01/2009 and in view of Sections 17(2) and Rule 12(b) of the said Act, no prosecution can be maintainable as against these petitioners who are admittedly the directors of the said Private Limited Company.
Mr. Roy has also relied up the decisions of the Apex Court as reported in 1983 SCC (Cri) 115 (Municipal Corporation of Delhi Vs. Ram Kishan Rohtagi And Others), (2011) 1 SCC (Cri) 8 (Pepsico India Holdings Private Limited Vs. Food Inspector And Another) and 1992 SCC (Cri) 412 (R.
Banerjee And Others Vs. H. D. Dubey And Others) in support of his claim that if the company nominates any person under Rule 12(b) of the said Act, then only the said person will be responsible for the conduct of the business of the said company and the directors cannot be arraigned for any Pawan Kumar Surana & Ors vs Bishnu Prasad Samanta on 12 January, 2017 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/15810846/
1 offence committed under the said Act.

sentences.text: It is submitted by Mr. Das, learned Advocate, representing the Kolkata Municipal Corporation by taking me to paragraph 16 of the application to convince this court that one petition was filed before the learned trial court by the petitioner no. 3 that some goods were purchased by that hotel from Anand Trading Company.
He submitted that under Section 14A of the said Act, this petitioner no. 3 tried to escape the legal liability.
Mr. Das contended that the said petition has not been annexed and that was necessary for appreciation of this application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.

He further contended that no copy of the resolution of the meeting of the company held on 22/12/2008 was produced before the learned trial court or the said resolution was not annexed with the Form No.
VIII (Annexure-P-4).
He further submitted that there is no address of the said Joydeep Nath appearing in that Form No. VIII.

In reply, it is submitted by Mr. Roy that the name of Joydeep Nath is very much there in the said Form as Operation Head of M/s. Middleton Hotels Pvt. Ltd. and that is enough address to track a person.

I have taken into consideration the argument put forward by the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the parties and the provisions of Section 17(2) of the said Act of 1954 and also the decisions cited by Mr. Roy.

I have given my anxious thought to running page 20, i.e. Annexure P-4 wherefrom it is clear that the accused no. 1, the company, M/s. Middleton Hotels Pvt. Ltd. as per resolution dated 22/12/2008 appointed one Joydeep Nath, the Operation Head of the said company to be in charge and responsible to the said company for the conduct of the business of the said company or establishment etc.
This was received by the Chief Municipal Health Officer, Kolkata Municipal Corporation on 01/01/2009 and the complaint was filed on 02/06/2010.
The argument of Mr. Das that no copy of such resolution of the company was annexed with the said Form No. VIII is belied by one sentence 'a certificate of the said resolution is enclosed'.
Thus, this court is satisfied that while lodging this complaint, the complainant did not take care of that Form No.VIII which was already before the municipal authority as back as on 02/01/2009.

In view of the specific intention of the legislature as enacted in Section 17(2) of the said Act, this court is satisfied that neither the Directors nor the Accountant who are the petitioners before this court ought not to have been roped in respect of the charge under Section 16(1)(a)(i) of the said Act, 1954.

The decision of Kerala High Court as reported in 2010 Cr.L.J. (NOC) 496 Kerala is not enough to give a go-bye to the three decisions of the Apex Court as referred to above which are squarely on the point as involved in this case.

This court is satisfied that further prosecution against these three accused persons will be against the interest of justice and no result can come out of this legal battle in view of the bar under Section 17(2) of the said Act, 1954.

sentences.text: Thus, exercising the inherent power granted to this court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, this court prefers to quash the further proceeding in respect of these three accused persons.
Liberty is, however, given to the Kolkata Municipal Corporation to rope in that Joydeep Nath, the Operation Head of the accused no.1/company forthwith so that the trial may not be stalled.
Let a copy of this order be forwarded to the learned trial court at once.
The criminal revisional application is, thus, disposed of.
All connected applications, if any, also stand disposed of.
Interim order, if any, is vacated.
Photostat certified copy of this order, if applied for, be supplied to the parties on usual undertaking.

(Indrajit Chatterjee, J.)
